title: Expose fail-closed tenant capability eligibility and staged governed remediation

phases.objective: Project canonical Platform Plugin resolver decisions into tenant-safe eligibility, bind staged managed repair to the existing Managed Execution input contract, and define an exact source-only dry-run authority path that remains blocked until Migration 1052 metadata and a non-expired dispatch-only Runtime Dispatch Certification exist.

e2e_journeys.actor: Authenticated tenant user resolving a Platform Plugin capability
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: POST /tenant/platform/plugins/resolve after canonical User-JWT and active-membership authorization
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The tenant response remains fail-closed and managed_repair.available remains false. Source-only dry-run code validates canonical User-JWT tenant/user/workspace authority, builds an immutable Managed Execution dry-run input, and permits that exact managed_operation authority only when the staged route-family metadata, exact non-expired dispatch-only runtime certification, and existing operate-or-stronger resource grant all validate. No certification is issued, no route is mounted, no run is created, and no external mutation occurs in this phase.
steps: Resolve the requested capability through the existing canonical Platform Plugin resolver and its fail-closed security gates.
Strip the admin-only decision trace projection from the tenant response as before.
Project required denied or unevaluated gates into tenant-safe blocker codes and repair classes without reading secrets or executing a repair.
Return ready only when the canonical resolver reports execution.will_execute=true.
Preserve inactive or otherwise non-executable bindings as their actual blocker state; only explicit action_binding_not_found and tool_binding_not_found are classified as missing binding.
Never treat the request selector echo as a canonical repair identity; derive action_key or tool_key only from the resolved binding row.
Withhold staged candidate metadata for missing bindings because no resolved binding exists to prove a canonical selector.
For missing or expired smoke certification, expose staged candidate metadata only when the resolved binding supplies the exact canonical selector.
Prefer the canonical plugin key from the resolved plugin row when deriving the candidate identity.

Hash only the canonical plugin key plus canonical selector for affected_operation.identity_sha256; expose blocker codes separately so the operation identity stays stable across remediation state transitions.
Keep managed_repair.available=false and omit executable repair requests while the dedicated executor is not registered and certified.
Resolve dry-run tenant/user authority from authenticated User-JWT membership context, never from resolver-result or request identity echoes.
Validate requested workspace membership through Context Kernel AuthorizedScopeRepository before using it as execution context.

Validate workspace ownership through Context Kernel WorkspaceOwnershipRepository; personal workspaces require the authenticated user to be the owner and company workspaces require active authorized scope.
Allow the source-only dry-run executor to preview only certify_platform_plugin_operation for a resolver-bound canonical smoke-certification blocker.

Build the Managed Execution binding from authenticated tenant/user/workspace identity, an explicit parent_ticket_id, the canonical operation identity, and the allowlisted dry-run repair operations only.

Derive one deterministic platform_plugin_operation resource_ref and one deterministic managed-execution idempotency key; transport request/correlation IDs cannot alter the run identity or managed_execution_input_hash.
Bind the future invocation to the internal createManagedExecutionRun service and explicitly forbid using the backend-only /managed-execution-runs HTTP route as the tenant integration seam.

Normalize execution_mode explicitly at the Managed Execution envelope boundary; live remains the backward-compatible default, dry_run is explicit, and conflicting top-level versus input_json modes fail closed.
Keep effect_class=managed_operation and execution_mode=dry_run rather than weakening authority semantics by pretending the repair is read_only.

Recognize the dry-run authority exception only when workflow_key, capability_key, resource_type, effect_class and execution_mode all exactly match the canonical tenant Platform Plugin managed-repair contract.

Require the staged route-family capability row to retain resource authority, audit, readback and the canonical tenant_platform_plugin_managed_repair_authority evidence requirement even though its base dispatch/apply flags remain disabled.

Require exactly one Runtime Dispatch Certification whose certification key, surface key and target key match the managed-repair dry-run contract, whose status is active/certified, whose dispatch_allowed=1 and apply_allowed=0, and whose dry-run/resource-authority/audit/readback flags and bounded evidence are present.
Require a valid future certification expiry and normalize certification timestamps before persisting the immutable Managed Execution authority snapshot.
Continue requiring an existing exact platform_plugin_operation or workspace grant with operate-or-stronger permission; the repair path cannot create or broaden its own resource authority.

Re-resolve both resource authority and the exact dry-run certification before privileged managed steps; certification rotation, evidence change or expiry fails closed through authority drift/revalidation.
Keep the generic Managed Execution apply gate unchanged for live mode, other workflows, other capabilities and every non-exact managed-operation path.
Keep run_creation_allowed=false and run_created=false because this source phase issues no certification, applies no migration and invokes no Managed Execution service.
Keep target authority, credential, approval, skill and canonical-policy blockers outside this dry-run executor so remediation cannot grant itself authority or credentials.
Keep Migration 1052 metadata-only with apply_allowed_default=0, enforcement_status=baseline_registered and executor_registered=0 until separately governed application/readback.

Require a later governed activation for Migration 1052 state verification, trusted internal certification issuance, actual internal run creation, reconciliation/final eligibility readback and representative Production canary evidence.
assertions: A dispatch-ready canonical resolver decision projects to status=ready with zero blockers.

Missing action/tool binding remains platform_admin_required with managed_repair.available=false and reason=canonical_plugin_operation_identity_required because the request selector is not canonical evidence.
Differently cased request selectors cannot create distinct staged repair identities when no resolved binding exists.
Missing/expired smoke certification with a resolved canonical binding remains platform_admin_required and managed_repair.available=false while exposing only staged candidate metadata.
Staged candidate selector identity is taken from result.binding.action_key or result.binding.tool_key, never from result.selector or requested_* key casing.
affected_operation.identity_sha256 remains stable for the same canonical plugin+selector when blocker codes change, while blocker_codes continue to reflect the current remediation state.
Inactive bindings are not rewritten as missing bindings and never become managed repair candidates.
If canonical plugin+selector identity is unavailable, the blocker remains platform_admin_required fail-closed.
The canonical resolved plugin key takes precedence over caller-supplied equivalent casing when deriving candidate identity.
Disabled and deprecated plugins never expose an available managed repair plan.
Missing credential projects to blocked + user_action_required with credential/OAuth intake guidance only.
Multiple eligible connection ambiguity projects to blocked + tenant_admin_action_available and never selects a first candidate.
Target resource authority remains platform_admin_required and is never auto-granted by managed repair.
No executable request template, idempotency key, caller-supplied tenant_id/user_id or workspace-dependent readback request is emitted by tenant eligibility discovery.
The dry-run preview rejects admin/backend principals and requires authenticated tenant_id, user_id and verified workspace_id context.
Caller or resolver-result identity echoes cannot replace authenticated tenant/user/workspace authority.
Requested workspace must exist in the authenticated user's Context Kernel authorized scope.
Personal workspace dry-run authority fails closed when owner_user_id differs from the authenticated user.
Unclassified workspace ownership fails closed.
Only certify_platform_plugin_operation is allowlisted for this source-only dry-run executor.
The same principal, canonical operation and repair operation set produces a deterministic preview fingerprint independent of request ID.
Managed Execution binding requires parent_ticket_id but derives tenant_id, user_id and workspace_id only from authenticated context.

Managed Execution binding uses workflow_key=tenant_platform_plugin_managed_repair_v1, the canonical managed-repair capability key, resource_type=platform_plugin_operation, effect_class=managed_operation and explicit top-level plus nested execution_mode=dry_run.
Conflicting or unsupported Managed Execution execution modes fail closed before authority resolution.
The same authenticated principal, parent ticket and canonical operation produce the same idempotency key and managed_execution_input_hash even when transport request/correlation IDs change.
The staged resource identity is deterministic and no resource grant or authority is created by the binding contract.
The binding names createManagedExecutionRun as the internal service, sets direct_http_route_allowed=false, and never invokes it in this phase.
Exact managed-repair dry-run authority can use dispatch-only certification while base route-family dispatch/apply flags remain false, but effective apply remains false.
Missing, ambiguous, inactive, expired, apply-enabled or incomplete dry-run certification fails closed.
An operate-or-stronger existing resource grant remains mandatory after certification succeeds.
Live mode or a non-canonical workflow cannot use the managed-repair dry-run exception and retains the generic Managed Execution capability/apply gates.
Dry-run certification evidence and timestamps are part of the immutable authority snapshot and are revalidated before managed steps; changed certification evidence produces authority drift.
The dry-run source still reports source_executor_implemented=true, executor_registered=false, apply_allowed=false and dispatch_apply_allowed=false until later activation.
No Runtime Dispatch Certification issuance, Managed Execution run, authority or credential creation, migration application, provider call, Production mutation or external write is performed.
Migration 1052 remains staged with dispatch/apply blocked and executor_registered=0.
A pending governed approval projects to approval_required rather than ready.
